steps.name: Confidence audit: power, method concordance, permutation null
caveats: With only 6 samples the permutation null is coarse and some permuted splits partially align with the true grouping, which makes the null conservative (inflated); say so rather than treating it as an exact FDR calibration.

Post-hoc power computed from the same data that produced the effect estimates is circular if used to argue a null result is a true null — report it as a detectable-effect floor, not as evidence of absence.
edgeR QLF is typically more conservative than DESeq2 at n=3; a smaller edgeR call set is expected and is not evidence that DESeq2 is wrong.
Leave-one-out at n=3 leaves n=2 in one group, where dispersion estimation is barely identifiable — use it only for relative stability ranking.
steps.context: The research question explicitly asks how confident one can be with three replicates per group; this step is the answer to that half. The enumeration of splits is small and exhaustive — 6 choose 3 = 20 ordered assignments, 10 unordered splits, so 9 non-identity permutations — so no sampling approximation is needed. edgeR and limma are both confirmed installed alongside DESeq2.
steps.question: How much confidence do 3 treated vs 3 control samples actually support — what effect size is detectable at the observed dispersion, does an independent method agree on the call set, and how many 'significant' genes does a label-permuted null produce?
constraints: Reuse the exact filtered gene set and count matrix from T1S1 for every method and every permutation so the comparisons are like-for-like.
Enumerate all 9 non-identity 3-vs-3 splits exhaustively; do not random-sample permutations.
Report the permutation null as a distribution of significant-gene counts alongside the observed count, and state plainly if the observed count falls inside the null range.
Frame all power statements as post-hoc and conditional on observed dispersion — do not report an 'achieved power' number for the observed effect sizes as if it were a design-stage power calculation.
For leave-one-out, report explicitly that the resulting 3-vs-2 comparisons are weaker than the primary analysis and are used only for stability assessment, never as an alternative primary result.
Use TMM normalization for edgeR and voom weights for limma rather than importing DESeq2 size factors, so the methods stay genuinely independent in their normalization.
steps.description: Quantify the statistical confidence the design supports, using the DESeq2 object and results from T1S1. Four components. (1) Dispersion and detectable effect: summarize the fitted gene-wise and trended dispersion estimates (median, quartiles, distribution across expression deciles) and translate them into a post-hoc detectable-effect curve — for n=3 per group at the observed library depth and observed dispersion quantiles, what minimum |log2FC| reaches padj<0.05 as a function of baseMean. Do this empirically from the observed data (e.g. by inverting the Wald statistic at the observed lfcSE per expression bin) rather than with a generic idealized power formula, and state that the estimate is post-hoc and conditional on the observed dispersions. (2) Independent-method concordance: re-run the same contrast with edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test (glmQLFit/glmQLFTest, TMM normalization) and with limma-voom, on the identical filtered gene set, and report the overlap of the FDR<0.05 call sets as a 3-way Venn/UpSet plus rank correlation (Spearman) of the test statistics. Concordance across methods is the practical confidence readout at small n. (3) Permutation null: enumerate all 3-vs-3 label assignments other than the true one (there are 9 distinct non-identity splits of 6 samples into two groups of 3, i.e. 10 splits total including the truth), re-run the DESeq2 Wald test for each, and report the number of genes at padj<0.05 per permuted labelling against the true labelling. This gives an empirical sense of how many hits the design manufactures under the null. (4) Robustness: leave-one-sample-out re-analysis (6 runs, each n=3 vs n=2 or n=2 vs n=3), reporting how many of the true-label significant genes survive each dropout, to identify hits driven by a single sample. Produce a short quantitative verdict on confidence, with numbers, not adjectives.
acceptance_criteria: Table and plot of fitted dispersion estimates by expression decile, with median dispersion and the corresponding biological coefficient of variation reported.
A detectable-effect curve giving minimum |log2FC| reachable at padj<0.05 versus baseMean for n=3 per group at the observed dispersions, with the post-hoc caveat stated in the output.
DESeq2 / edgeR-QLF / limma-voom three-way overlap of FDR<0.05 gene sets, plus Spearman correlation of test statistics between methods.
Significant-gene counts under all 9 permuted 3-vs-3 labellings, tabulated against the true-label count.
Leave-one-sample-out stability table: for each of the 6 dropouts, the fraction of the original significant genes retained.
A written verdict quantifying confidence — including how many hits, if any, are supported by all three methods and survive every leave-one-out run.

steps.name: Rank-based pathway enrichment of the treatment response
caveats: Enrichment on a 3-vs-3 contrast inherits that contrast's noise: a significant NES is a statement about coordinate rank shift, not about pathway activity, and must not be reported as mechanism.
GO BP sets are nested and heavily overlapping, so blocks of correlated significant terms are expected; collapse them before counting.
WikiPathways sets vary widely in size and curation depth; small sets are unstable at this sample size.
If the gene-level analysis produced few or no significant genes, a significant GSEA result is a weak coordinated shift, not a rescue of the gene-level null — say so.
steps.context: The dataset is human liver (taxon 9606) with HGNC gene symbols as row identifiers, so human symbol-keyed GMT collections apply directly with no ortholog mapping. Confirmed staged human collections: MSigDB hallmark (50 sets), MSigDB GO BP/CC/MF, and WikiPathways human. Restrict the GSEA universe to the genes actually tested in T1S1 so set sizes and p-values reflect the real background rather than the full genome.
steps.question: Which biological processes and pathways are coordinately shifted in treated versus control human liver samples, and does the pathway-level signal hold up better than the gene-level one at n=3?
constraints: Rank on the full tested gene list from T1S1 — do not pre-filter to significant genes before GSEA.
Use human gene-set collections only; the mouse and rat collections staged in this environment must not be used on these human liver samples.
Intersect every gene set with the tested-gene background and report post-intersection set sizes; drop sets with fewer than 10 or more than 500 background genes.
Set a fixed random seed for the permutation-based enrichment and report it.
Report adjusted p-values (BH across sets within each collection separately), never nominal p-values alone.
If a named collection cannot be resolved at run time, report which one was missing and proceed with the collections that did resolve — do not substitute a different organism's sets.
Handle duplicated gene symbols in the ranking by keeping the entry with the largest absolute statistic, and report how many duplicates were collapsed.
steps.description: Run gene-set enrichment on the full ranked gene list from T1S1 (all filtered genes ranked by the DESeq2 Wald statistic, or by -log10(p) signed by log2FC — state which and use one consistently), rather than on a thresholded DE list, because rank-based aggregation retains power when per-gene calls are sparse. Use human gene-set collections matched to this dataset's HGNC gene symbols: the hallmark collection as the primary readout, GO Biological Process for mechanism-level resolution, and WikiPathways human for curated pathway context — all three are staged human resources in this environment. Report normalized enrichment scores, nominal and BH-adjusted p-values, leading-edge genes, and set sizes after intersecting with the 12,000-gene background. Additionally, for context only, run over-representation analysis on the padj<0.05 DE list if that list has at least 15 genes, and state clearly if it does not. Cross-reference the leading-edge genes of the top pathways against the multi-method-concordant gene list from T1S2 and report what fraction of each pathway's leading edge is method-robust.
acceptance_criteria: GSEA results tables for hallmark, GO-BP and WikiPathways human, each with NES, nominal p, BH-adjusted p, set size after background intersection, and leading-edge gene lists.
An enrichment plot (dot or bar) of the top significantly enriched sets per collection, or an explicit statement that no set reached adjusted p<0.05 in that collection.
GO-BP results collapsed for parent/child redundancy before any count of 'number of enriched processes' is reported.
Over-representation analysis on the padj<0.05 DE list, or an explicit statement that the list was too small (<15 genes) to support ORA.
For the top enriched sets, the fraction of leading-edge genes that were called by all three methods in T1S2.

plan.title: Liver drug-treated vs control DE with n=3 power audit
plan.analytical_narrative: The input is a single small bulk RNA-seq experiment: /data/inputs/counts/counts.csv holds raw integer Salmon gene-level counts for 12,000 gene symbols x 6 samples (7 columns = gene symbol + 6 samples), with /data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv giving one condition label per sample — 3 treated vs 3 control, unpaired, single batch, human liver. The research question has two halves and the plan mirrors them. First, identify the differentially expressed genes: T1S1 builds the DESeq2 object, does QC (library sizes, VST PCA/correlation clustering, outlier screening via Cook's distance) and the negative-binomial Wald test for treated vs control, with apeglm/ashr LFC shrinkage because with 3 vs 3 the unshrunken log2FC of low-count genes is dominated by noise. Second, and equally important given the explicit framing of the question, T1S2 quantifies how much confidence n=3 supports: it reports the dispersion estimates DESeq2 actually fitted, runs an empirical post-hoc power/detectable-effect calculation at the observed dispersions and sequencing depth, cross-checks the DE call set against an independent method (edgeR quasi-likelihood, which is the more conservative FDR control at tiny n) to report call-set concordance, and runs a permutation/label-swap null (all 9 non-identity 3-3 splits) to show the false-positive rate the design carries. That concordance-plus-null pair is the honest answer to 'how confident can we be', not a p-value narrative. T1S3 then runs pathway-level analysis on the full ranked gene list rather than a thresholded list, because gene-set aggregation is the part of the analysis that survives low replication best; it uses the staged human hallmark, GO-BP and WikiPathways human collections (all confirmed present under /mnt/refs and matched to Homo sapiens). No batch term is possible or needed (single batch); no pairing term (unpaired). Nothing in the question touches drug targets, safety or clinical outcome data, so no translational steps are added.
